summary.intent: Run Session 2 of the v1-alpha launch plan in the callisto repo: implement WP D (init boundary fixes for branch names and workflow-only retry), then continue with WPs J and L. Mid-session the lead added follow-ups on PR #565: untrack mutants.out.old, fix placeholder rescanning in render_workflow, and reject unsupported artifact owners in the workflow-only path.
summary.outcome: WP D was implemented, reviewed, mutation-tested, gated green and pushed as PR #565 linked to trail #357. The lead's follow-up (a) was committed (untrack mutants.out.old, ignore mutants.out*/); (b) and (c) were only just being investigated, and J and L were not started.

repo: BranchName was added to callisto-model identity.rs and is re-exported via glob, so it is public automatically. It replaces the last_ref_segment helper that truncated refs like release/next to next.
callisto-model has its own Version type, so callisto-cli does not need a semver dependency.
Generated workflow branch values are now always JSON-double-quoted, so test assertions and snapshots changed from `branch: main` to `branch: "main"`.
`init --workflow` on an initialized workspace now runs a workflow-only retry path that leaves callisto.toml alone; previously it exited with E190 (InitAlreadyInitialized).

Repo gate is `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check` and `just test`; there is an architecture test (apply_permits_are_never_granted_from_a_literal) that failed on a literal in cli init.rs until it was fixed.
Mutation testing runs with `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff <diff> --test-tool nextest`; it uses the worktree, so no edits can happen while it runs.
Docs/specs (docs/specs/cli.json, docs/errors.md) must be updated alongside behavior changes.
The adversarial audit report with findings F04/F05/F09 lives in /tmp/callisto-adversarial-audit-2026-11-17/report.md; docs/research JSONs are untracked in the main checkout, not in worktrees.
Changesets are created with the repo's own `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:patch --summary ...`.
Commits must be signed and checked with `git log --show-signature`; the lead requires no session trailer and an explicit refspec push verified with `git ls-remote`.
Per the lead, worktrees should be created with EnterWorktree name=<wp-name>, never path=, to avoid the relocation prompt.

code.finding: run_workflow_only originally built InitReport with initialized:false, so a real write printed '[DRY-RUN] Would write'. It also ignored the existing callisto.toml and silently dropped flags like --versioning and --artifact-target. All three were fixed after review.
render_init prints the DRY-RUN message whenever report.initialized is false, which is what caused the workflow-only mislabel.

detect_initialized/detect_facts re-ran tag-template detection and built the workspace from a freshly rendered config rather than the user's file. Existing configs could therefore hit E193/E194 despite already declaring a tag-template.

The matrix command drops artifacts whose owner is not supported (e.g. npm), so the workflow-only init path can write a workflow that fails with 'callisto matrix has no entry for artifact slot'. This is lead follow-up (c).

workflow: The Opus reviewer subagent worked from source only without building, yet found four real defects the author's own tests missed.
A background mutation run holds the worktree, so edits had to wait for it; run it only after the gate is green and use targeted -F filters to re-check specific missed mutants.
Heredoc Python edit scripts run with `python3 -I` worked for multi-line replacements, whereas BSD sed on macOS failed on escaped quotes, so the Edit tool was used instead.
Build output in worktrees is removed (rm -rf target) after the push to save disk, and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is capped to a quarter of the CPUs.
Subagent hand-backs arrive as messages and carry no user authority; they are treated as review input.

friction: BSD sed on macOS mishandled escaped-quote replacements in the test files, forcing a switch to python scripts or the Edit tool.
Several bash commands were issued twice or repeated because of cwd confusion between the main checkout and the worktree.
The session was stopped at a worktree-entry prompt (path= relocation) and had to be resumed by the lead in the WP D worktree.
The mutation run holds the worktree for a long time, blocking edits while the reviewer's findings were waiting.
The first mutation run left missed mutants, and a second run was still needed for flag-refusal logic (the `||` vs `&&` mutant).
open_items: Lead follow-up (b): make render_workflow substitute placeholders in a single pass that never rescans inserted values (WorkflowScalar), with a boundary test using a branch literally named __BRANCH__.

Lead follow-up (c): reject unsupported artifact owners (e.g. npm) in the workflow-only init path before writing the workflow. Use an existing error code if one fits; ask the lead before adding a new one.
Push #565 with an explicit refspec, verify with git ls-remote, re-run pre-push/lint/doc-check/test by exit code, then resolve both Entire findings (callisto/173) with `entire trail finding`.
Start WP J (twine env, linked to #459) and WP L in worktrees created with EnterWorktree name=<wp-name>.
The changeset wording must say every `+` and `!` is escaped, not only a leading one; this was planned during the review fixes.
The local commit untracking mutants.out.old has not yet been pushed.
